text:
ingrid: noticing a p95/p99 jump on hosted inference for text-generation-xxl after last night's kernel push. p95 went from ~230ms -> ~480ms, p99 from ~540ms -> ~1.1s. started at ~02:10 UTC. rolling canary shows same.

aj: yikes. which change landed? commit?

ingrid: deploy 2395 (runtime rev c12f8a) — enabled SDPA path and set prefer_flash=true in compile flags. change set by build job: 
```
CFLAGS="-O3 -march=native -DUSE_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 -DENABLE_SDPA=1"
cmake .. && ninja
```

sourabh: did you repro locally with the same model + sequence lengths? could be long-context kernel fallback thrashing.

ingrid: repro steps below (shared to save time):
```bash
# reproduce (single request)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-generation-xxl","input":"repeat word "*2000","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0}' \
```
Observed latencies: 
- baseline (before c12f8a): p95=220ms p99=540ms
- after c12f8a: p95=480ms p99=1108ms

aj: can you paste the runtime logs around kernel selection? the engine logs kernel/attention selection decisions.

ingrid: pasted snippet from node-17 logs (canary):
```
[02:11:02.132] model=text-generation-xxl seq=2048 selecting_kernel: sdpa_enabled=true flash_candidate=true kernel=flash_attn_v2 latency_est=0.18ms
[02:11:02.133] kv_cache: hit_prefix=0 use_contiguous_kv=true
[02:11:02.134] exec: fallback_to_sdpa: kernel_runtime_error=not_enough_shared_mem
[02:11:02.135] exec: fallback_kernel=sdpa_fused_softmax latency_est=0.56ms
[02:11:02.190] exec: actual_step_time=0.48ms
[02:11:03.742] request=abc123 end p95=480ms p99=1108ms
```

sourabh: looks like a pathological mix: kernel picks flash path, then runtime hits "not_enough_shared_mem" and falls back to SDPA which is slower for this seq shape. fallback thrash + JIT/compilation overhead could add 200-500ms.

maria: can we force-disable flash_attn for the affected CUDA arch in the short term? e.g. runtime flag `--kernel-prefer=sdpa` or env `FORCE_FLASH=0` so the selection doesn't flip mid-request.

aj: good call. also check the kernel cache on nodes — the JIT for flash might be compiling on first use. if many concurrent cold compiles, p99 spikes. we should check `nvtx` traces and /var/tmp/flash_jit_cache.

ingrid: quick mitigation applied: set env on canary pool `RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=sdpa_prefer` and disabled SDPA experimental flag in build config for new builds. initial numbers after env flip: p95 -> 240ms, p99 -> 560ms. :relieved:

ops-bot: Deploy 2396 started for canary pool (runtime rev c12f8a+hotfix) by ingrid — flags: RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=sdpa_prefer

aj: nice. long-term we need better kernel scoring: consider penalizing fallbacks by adding compile-time check of shared memory footprint and precomputing which kernels are valid for a given (model, seq_len, batch). also keep a precompiled cache per arch to avoid cold JIT.

sourabh: agree. plan: (1) add pre-flight kernel eligibility check in kernel selector, (2) persist flash_jit artifacts to network cache, (3) add telemetry counter for "fallback_occurred" and correlate with p99. I'll sketch the change.

maria: also add a runtime override in Console per-deployment so SREs can toggle kernel preference without a full redeploy — feature flag UI + API.

ingrid: for the immediate customer-facing incident, I opened support ticket #INC-3262 and notified the top 5 tenants on the canary that may have seen latency increases. will keep the canary pinned to sdpa_prefer until we validate precompiled flash artifacts.

aj: for reproduction/diagnostics, two more commands that were helpful:
```bash
# tail realtime kernel selection decisions
ssh node-17 'journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f | grep kernel_selection'

# check JIT cache entries
ls -lh /var/tmp/flash_jit_cache | tail
```

sourabh: initial design notes I'll add to the runtime PR: summary, fallback cost model, precompilation step, metrics to emit (kernel_choice, fallback_reason, compile_time_ms, is_jit_compiled). will include sample query for Console: `sum(rate(kernel_selector_fallback_total[5m])) by (model)`

ingrid: testing notes from canary after hotfix (10m window):
- request mix: 90% seq<=512, 10% seq>1024
- p95 overall: 245ms (down from 480ms)
- p99 overall: 570ms (down from 1108ms)
- fallback counter dropped from 32/min -> 1/min

maria: good progress. next steps: roll hotfix to 10% prod on Monday, run heavy seq concurrency test (100 concurrent seq=2048 requests) in staging, and implement precompile cache within 2 sprints. I'll file tracking tickets.

aj: sounds like a plan. thanks everyone for fast turnaround. :thumbsup:

ingrid: closing loop here — will paste postmortem draft into #postmortems once we've got the telemetry and the PRs. thanks!
